Go standard library notes: strings.Fields and strconv.Atoi

strings.Fields divides a string wherever runs of Unicode whitespace occur.
Leading and trailing whitespace does not produce empty entries. The result is
a slice of strings, useful when reading words or numbers from a line.

strconv.Atoi interprets a string as a decimal integer of the platform's int
size. It returns the integer and an error; callers should handle the error
rather than assuming every token is numeric.

package demo

import (
    "strconv"
    "strings"
)

func FirstInteger(line string) (int, error) {
    words := strings.Fields(line)
    return strconv.Atoi(words[0]) // The caller supplies at least one word.
}

This illustrative snippet describes library APIs, without defining any
exercise-specific data structure or solving a matrix task.
